section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-pilgrim_road — FAITH → WAR
text: {settlement} read the {route} as {counterpart}'s artery (through the picture of the web it holds, which is not the web there is) and cut it. The picture sits in the record beside the cutting, and the walk will not tidy it afterwards.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-pilgrim_road — FAITH → WAR
text: An intercepted column is two entries: a grievance in the war ledger and a sacred tension on the faith axis, scored separately and both standing. The war that opens carries the road on its reasons, and the peace that closes it will have to say the road's name out loud.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-pilgrim_road — FAITH → WAR
text: {npc} went down the {route} with the season's column and into the foreign-guest hold at {settlement}. The hold has one writer and a long memory, and {counterpart} has been told.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-pilgrim_road — FAITH → WAR
text: The road opened again by agreement and not by war. {counterpart} came to {settlement} with a term for the season's passage; {settlement} signed it; and the pilgrims went up the {route} under a clause instead of an escort, which is the only shape this counterforce has ever been receipted in.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-pilgrim_road — FAITH → WAR
text: {settlement} interdicted the {route} used by pilgrims travelling to {counterpart}; a war was opened whose recorded reasons name the road.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-house_run — INFORMATION → TRADE
text: {house} is refused at {band} counters in one season, over a shortage nobody has seen.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-house_run — INFORMATION → TRADE
text: A story about {house}'s next {good} has done what an audit could not.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-house_run — INFORMATION → TRADE
text: {house}'s books broke under the refusals, and the refusals were each one reasonable.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-house_run — INFORMATION → TRADE
text: The plant was aimed at the trade {house} is known for (their {good} is short, their next deliveries will fail), and it was priced into the market before it was believed anywhere in particular. Every creditor who then refused a renewal did so on their own reading, and each refusal is its own reasonable page.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-house_run — INFORMATION → TRADE
text: The books broke under the refusals, in that order: the credibility fell because the payments failed, and not the other way about. The walk shows which came first, which is the only reason anyone knows it.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-house_run — INFORMATION → TRADE
text: The story reached {settlement} at the fourth hand and stopped there. It arrived alone and uncorroborated, the books were thick, and not one counter refused. The same plant, the same house, and nothing at all in the ledger.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-house_run — INFORMATION → TRADE
text: A planted report said {house}'s next {good} would fail to arrive; {house}'s creditors refused renewal, and {house}'s books failed.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-diaspora_return — POPULATIONS → WAR
text: The silver rebuilding {settlement} comes from the grandsons of the people who left it.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-diaspora_return — POPULATIONS → WAR
text: {counterpart}'s old-country ledger has funded a claim against the town that made the exodus.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-diaspora_return — POPULATIONS → WAR
text: The refounding of {settlement} was paid for by the season that emptied it.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-diaspora_return — POPULATIONS → WAR
text: They left in a bad season, and the departure entry named every destination they left toward. The memory was written at both ends and decays on a clock of its own; at {counterpart} it has not finished decaying. That is what made the funding possible, and the ledger says so in the plainest way: under obligations, generation upon generation.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-diaspora_return — POPULATIONS → WAR
text: The grudge travelled with the money. A lineage claim filed by a refounded child town is the same instrument as any other claim, sworn on a memory {timeband_age} and priced no differently for it.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-diaspora_return — POPULATIONS → WAR
text: The households at {counterpart} took up the host's rites and stopped entering {settlement} as home, and the funding stopped with the entering. The decay law says exactly when, and the ruin was raised by somebody else or not at all.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-diaspora_return — POPULATIONS → WAR
text: {settlement}'s people left for {counterpart} in a bad season; households at {counterpart} have since funded {settlement}'s refounding, and a claim has been filed from the refounded town.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-corner_and_mitre — TRADE → FAITH
text: The credit that raised {temple}'s new chapter came out of the hungry season at {settlement}.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-corner_and_mitre — TRADE → FAITH
text: {timeband_since}, {temple} is answering for whose money seated its minister.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-corner_and_mitre — TRADE → FAITH
text: {house} sold into the gap it had helped to make, and the fortune is entered with the stain.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-corner_and_mitre — TRADE → FAITH
text: No verb in a house's book endows a temple. Credit extended, relief granted at the temple's own grain in the season {house} made hungry, and a local faction propped through both: influence rode the ledger, and the contest was fought by people who owed.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-corner_and_mitre — TRADE → FAITH
text: The leash is foreign by construction ({house} sits a town over), and when the mark surfaced, the scandal sharpened against the creed rather than the merchant. That is not an injustice the model failed to notice. It is the reading the congregation made.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-corner_and_mitre — TRADE → FAITH
text: {temple} refused the credit at the door, reading the same provenance the stain would have ridden, and the contest was fought by people who owed nobody. The corner still happened. Only the mitre did not.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-corner_and_mitre — TRADE → FAITH
text: {house}, of {counterpart}, cornered {good} at {settlement} before a shortage and extended credit to {temple}; a minister at {temple} was later exposed as holding under {house}'s leash.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-rush_and_war — INFORMATION → WAR
text: {settlement} marches on a creek no one at its court has seen. The telling was enough.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-rush_and_war — INFORMATION → WAR
text: The strike at {settlement} grew with every telling, and the columns are converging on the last version of it.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-rush_and_war — INFORMATION → WAR
text: The wall at {settlement} turned {band} back with receipts, and the disappointment went home in letters.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-rush_and_war — INFORMATION → WAR
text: The find was real and small. Per relay the telling drifted, and the drift is the entire machinery. By the third hand the creek was a motherlode, and the pull that moved the columns was scored off the third hand and not the first.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-rush_and_war — INFORMATION → WAR
text: The war's own receipt confesses its epistemics: it names a misjudgment as the deciding term, in the entry, at the opening, and no clerk has softened it since.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-rush_and_war — INFORMATION → WAR
text: It dissolved the honest way. The letters home corrected the belief, the reckonings ground together, and the opener stopped being able to say the victim was rich. And the receipt names which of those ended it.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
kind: JF-SS-rush_and_war — INFORMATION → WAR
text: A resource strike at {settlement} was exaggerated in relay; two courts moved on the exaggerated report, and the war that opened dissolved when the belief was corrected.

kind: JF-W-grievance_to_war — WAR → WAR
text: {settlement} declares vengeance on {counterpart}, its weakened neighbour: {timeband} grudge will be met.

kind: JF-W-grievance_to_war — WAR → WAR
text: {timeband_since}, the incident on the {route} is a named reason in {settlement}'s war ledger.

kind: JF-W-grievance_to_war — WAR → WAR
text: A season of small entries against {counterpart} has crossed into one large one.

kind: JF-W-grievance_to_war — WAR → WAR
text: The entries accumulated in the ordinary way: a seizure, a refusal, a border reading, none of them a war on its own. The fold that reads them together crossed its bar. And the reasons pinned at the opening are the ones that were standing that week, not the ones the heralds have shouted since, which is why the two accounts differ.

kind: JF-W-grievance_to_war — WAR → WAR
text: A grievance decays if nothing feeds it, and the feeding is on the record: which season each entry landed, what fed it after, and which of them was still live at the open.

kind: JF-W-grievance_to_war — WAR → WAR
text: The pinned reasons are compared against the live fold at every re-read, and when the last of them has gone out of the fold the war has nothing left to be about. That, rather than a victory, is how most of them end, and the receipt names the term that did it.

kind: JF-W-grievance_to_war — WAR → WAR
text: {settlement} recorded grievances against {counterpart} and then opened war on them; {counterpart}'s recorded strength had fallen, and the reasons pinned at the opening are on the record.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: {settlement} has taken the other side of {counterpart}'s war, and the obligation it walked away from is entered at the severity a betrayal carries.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: {settlement} sits in the enemy's council now, and will pay for the chair through {timeband_span}.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: The word of the switch is still on the road: {third_party} is pricing {settlement} at what it was worth last season, and will not be for long.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: The tie between {settlement} and {counterpart} had worn {band} thin before it broke. A sound one could not have been crossed, and everyone at that table knows it.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: The tie eroded before it broke, and every step of the eroding is on the record: {settlement} stopped discharging, defaulted the obligation at the top band, and rode into the opposing web through the ordinary join read. No teleported entry, and no door but the one everybody uses. The entry that default made is what every court reads {timeband_since}, whenever it weighs taking {settlement} in.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: The turncoat receipt names both movements in one line, the leaving and the arriving. Beneath it the ingratitude debt sits unsettled on {counterpart}'s own pair ledger, feeding the grievance mass the war reasons read. The betrayal casus is derivable from that entry and from nothing else, which is why nobody had to invent one.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: A burial between {settlement} and {counterpart} closes the entry in their own two books and in no others. {third_party} still holds the row and still reads it at the join, and was never party to the peace that set it down, so the bar {settlement} must clear never quite comes back down.

kind: JF-W-ally_to_turncoat — WAR → WAR
text: {settlement} left {counterpart}'s coalition without settling its obligation and joined the opposing side; {counterpart} and its remaining allies have recorded a grievance against {settlement}.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: {third_party} moved on {settlement} on the right of answer it has held since {counterpart} burned: {timeband_since}, and paid in the same coin.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: They burned {counterpart} and rode home, and the one license their answer minted is already held somewhere else.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: {faction} calls the burning of {counterpart} an atrocity and is arming on it. A charge built out of what the roads carried.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: {settlement} weighed the web that would answer and did not strike: the license it would have minted was priced dearer than the town it would have taken.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: Before the torches, {settlement}'s captains priced the web that would answer, and marched regardless. {counterpart} burned; the world read it on its own axes, monumental in one hall and merely recognized in the next; and {timeband_since} the single license that answer minted was carried to the field by {third_party}, whose own quarrel with {settlement} had reached the same extreme. It was spent once, and it mints nothing back.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: The neighbours {settlement} meant to quiet did not all quiet. One road kept {timeband} caution and the next hall over entered the ash as a reason to arm. Terror working and terror backfiring, read off one record, one act and two ledgers, and the {temple} between them keeping a third account of it.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: The named of {counterpart} are not in the arithmetic. {band} went out as refugees down the roads the column came in on, the named cast among them; the roll that counts the dead does not count them and was never meant to; the tier fell because the truth fell and not because a second hand wrote it down; and the institutions stand as shells the clerks still list by name.

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning — WAR → WAR
text: {settlement} razed {counterpart} after a won siege; {counterpart}'s tier has fallen and its institutions are shells, and neighbouring settlements have recorded a claim against {settlement}.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} holds the {good} of {settlement}, and the crowd took the warehouse door off its hinges.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} kept the corner and lost the hall it sits in. The guilds moved on its own institutions while the gouge ran.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: The dear band {house} made was heard on every road, and the roads answered before the crowd could: wagons came into {settlement} from towns that had never sent one.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house}'s price stood against the petitions for exactly as long as they were only petitions.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: It began quietly, with {house} buying {good} wherever it was cheap and buying all of it, and it ended at the granary door: the reachable share crossed the band and the clerks entered the day; the sale book entered every load dear, and every entry was evidence; the guilds turned on {house}'s own institutions; and the crowd carried the stock to the public granary in daylight, load for load out of one book and into the town's.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: The seat reached the warehouse before the crowd did and ordered the {good} sold into the public granary at {band}. The wardens counted the sacks out while the town watched. {settlement} ate; {house} entered its grievance beside the stock; and the seat will be answering for that order long after the winter it answered.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: The corner advertised itself, which was always the flaw in it. The band was carried down every road out of {settlement}; wagons came off the {route} from towns with no custom there; the arrivals were entered against the held share; and {house} sold into the band it had broken and will be counting the difference through {timeband_span}.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: The corner ended and the name has outlasted it. The chronicle keeps the winter under {house}'s name and no clerk has moved it; the old carters date things from it, before and after; and {timeband_since} grandchildren of that queue refuse {house}'s custom without being able to say why.

kind: JF-T-corner_to_riot — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} held the reachable stock of {good} in {settlement} above the band and sold at a raised price; the crowd seized the warehouse stock and moved it into the public granary.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} lent to the seat of {settlement} and asked for the {route} in the terms; the debt is a grievance now, and the {route} with it.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: {counterpart} took the wagons and sent nothing back. The next bargain out of {settlement} will be dearer for it.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} has settled the debt and not the entry; the {settlement} wharf still prices the name {band} below what it took before.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: A merchant's broken word buys no march: {settlement} holds its grievance against {counterpart} and has nothing in the war book to set beside it.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: The credit was extended in a good season and called in a bad one. {counterpart} took the {good} and sent nothing back; the wharf waited for a cargo that never came and stopped waiting in the autumn; the book carried {counterpart} in the column of debts unanswered; and when the season turned again the severance was entered as a betrayal with {reason} on the record. A casus commercii, in the commerce ledger, where it stays.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: The default prices {counterpart} up in every join read that weighs taking it in, and draws the counter-coalition onto it, and hands {settlement} nothing whatever to march on. A commercial betrayer becomes hard to ally with and easy to gang up on. It does not thereby acquire a war reason, and no clerk in either town can make it one.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: The guild book records the default and the record outlives the money: {timeband_since} the debt is discharged and the entry is not, factors who once took {house}'s word ask for it in writing, and nobody has accused {house} of anything and nobody deals with it on a handshake either.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: The relief came first and is read last. {house} opened its granaries to {settlement} in a lean month and took no profit on it; the town called it kindness and the clerks entered it as a loss; and when the seat came asking again, both sides were reading the same entry and reading it differently, which is how a generous book becomes a disputed one without a word of it changing.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal — TRADE → TRADE
text: {settlement} extended credit to {counterpart} under the compact; {counterpart} did not repay what it owed in {good}, and {settlement} has recorded the default as a betrayal-class severance.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: The {house} venture is lost on the {route}, and the books that carried it stand at {band} by the end of the same season.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} staked its season on a band at {counterpart} it had heard and never seen; the {route} settled the question.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} is broken, not by one bad season, but by one bad season arriving after everything else.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} called the venture back before the second stage, sold the cargo where it stood, and kept its books; no ballad will be made of it.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: It was a modest proposal, as every ruin in the guild book was. The stake stood above {house}'s own standing practice with the reason entered as {reason}; the wagons went out heavy with {good} and half the quay came to watch them load; the news came back to the {settlement} quay before the season did, and came back alone. The stake was struck out with nothing set against it, and the books closed at the bottom band with the interests struck out one by one.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: The family survives the books. The name will trade again in somebody's grandchildren's time or it will not, and until then every bargain it asks for on this coast is priced against one voyage that did not come back.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: The partners did not go down with it. The marks that shared one tarpaulin are on other tarpaulins {timeband_since}, {faction} keeps books on the {settlement} quay where {house} kept them, and the carters have a choice of employers again and have discovered that they enjoy it.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: The joint stake had a second failure inside it: {faction} did not put in its share and {house} carried the venture alone, the unpaid share entered against {faction} in {house}'s book and in the guild's. When the road took the venture, {house} was ruined by the road and {faction} by the entry, and only one of those two can be argued about.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin — TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} staked a venture above its standing practice and the venture failed on the {route}; {house}'s holdings and credit have both fallen, and its interests at {settlement} have been struck out.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: The render at {settlement} outran the piety that paid it, and the temple it paid for keeps two congregations now.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: {temple}'s render came in whole while the benches thinned under it, and the two facts sat a season apart in the same book.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: The tithe dispute went to {counterpart} for arbitration and came back a schism {timeband_since}.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: {settlement} had no room for a second rite: the weaker congregation was evicted, and the split closed as fast as it opened because the slots were never there for it.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: It began as a question of what the render was owed on: {npc} and the steward could not agree, the legate was sent for, and {faction} was calling it a tax dispute while the unaffiliated rolls grew the whole time the argument ran. When it broke, it broke along the altar. The old rite keeps the nave and the new keeps the crypt, both halves claim {creed}, and the roster carries a congregation for {rival_creed} that is impaired, tolerated, and very much alive.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: The capacity floor is the whole difference between a schism and a suppression. Where the slots existed, {settlement} lives with two congregations under one roof and no agreement about the roof; where they did not, {temple} absorbed what was left of the other, and nobody calls that a reconciliation.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: The render had been forgiven once at {settlement}, in a worse year than this one, and the parish had not forgotten it. The new demand was read against that entry, which is why the argument went to the altar instead of to the steward, and why {temple} could not settle it by explaining the arithmetic.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: Neither half calls itself the new thing. Both claim {creed}, both keep the calendar, both send to the same chapter house, and the register at {settlement} will be carrying two entries under one name {timeband_since}, under a clerk's note nobody has ever settled.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism — FAITH → FAITH
text: {temple} raised the render at {settlement} and the parish disputed it; the congregation has split, and {settlement}'s institution roster now carries a second congregation.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground — FAITH → FAITH
text: {creed} was put down at {settlement}, and the undercroft gave it back {timeband_since}.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground — FAITH → FAITH
text: {settlement}'s seat made {creed}'s punishment public and gave {reason} for it, and the crowd that came to watch is what {creed} has grown by since.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground — FAITH → FAITH
text: The register held {creed} extinct at {settlement}; the doors of {temple} opened {timeband_since} and what walked out was not strangers.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground — FAITH → FAITH
text: It was found the ordinary way: a talkative neighbour, and then {faction} at the undercroft door. {npc} was taken up with the vessels, the seat has the names and is reading them off the market cross for {reason}, and a parish that had not thought about {creed} in years is thinking about very little else this week.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground — FAITH → FAITH
text: The purge was thorough and it was public, and both of those turned out to be the mistake. The crowd that came to watch stayed to listen; the pews filled in defiance; {creed}'s share at {settlement} has risen since. {faction} meant it as a warning, and it was received as an invitation.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground — FAITH → FAITH
text: The suppression lifted and the rite came up out of the cellars where it had been the whole time. The roster restores {creed} to standing, and the ministers who presented themselves were strangers to nobody. The entry calling it extinct is still in the book, uncorrected, directly above the entry that restores it.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground — FAITH → FAITH
text: {settlement} suppressed {creed} and struck its standing from the roster; {creed}'s rite was found still being kept at {settlement}, and those keeping it have been named.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy — FAITH → FAITH
text: The priests of {settlement} read the failed harvest as {creed}'s wrath, and named the season it would lift.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy — FAITH → FAITH
text: {npc} named {when}; {when} came and went, and {temple}'s standing at {settlement} fell for it.

kind: JF-SC-stab_in_the_back: WAR → INTERIOR

kind: JF-W-razing_to_reckoning: WAR → WAR

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal: TRADE → TRADE
text: The wharf at {settlement} waits for nothing out of {counterpart} and stopped waiting in the autumn, and the {good} that was owed is a thing the town says out loud to strangers.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal: TRADE → TRADE
text: Bargains at {settlement} are asked for in writing, and {timeband_since} the entry that made that the custom is still open.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal: TRADE → TRADE
text: The guild's older hands remember the relief that came first (granaries opened in a lean month at no profit, entered as a loss) and remember that both towns were reading the same entry and reading it differently the moment the seat came asking again.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal: TRADE → TRADE
text: A merchant's broken word buys no march: {settlement} has nothing in the war book to set beside the grievance, and no clerk in either town can make one out of what is there.

kind: JF-T-credit_to_betrayal: TRADE → TRADE
text: {timeband_since} the debt is discharged and the entry is not. Factors who once took {settlement}'s word ask for it in writing, nobody has accused the town of anything, and nobody takes its word without a clerk in the room.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin: TRADE → TRADE
text: {house}'s interests at {settlement} are struck out one by one and the books close at the bottom band; the stake that did it stood above the house's own standing practice, with {reason} entered beside it.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin: TRADE → TRADE
text: The quay at {settlement} talks about one loading and no other: half the town came out to watch those wagons go, and the news came back before the season did, and came back alone.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin: TRADE → TRADE
text: The counting-house on the quay carries {faction}'s mark; {house} kept its books there until the venture failed on the {route}, and the sign was changed without ceremony.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin: TRADE → TRADE
text: {timeband_since}, the old partners are on other tarpaulins, and the carters can pick an employer again, which is new here, and is spoken of as though it were weather.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin: TRADE → TRADE
text: The family outlives the books: every bargain the name asks for on this coast is priced against one voyage that did not come back, and will be until somebody's grandchildren are asking.

kind: JF-T-venture_to_ruin: TRADE → TRADE
text: {house} keeps its quay and its bands at {settlement} because somebody read the second stage and declined it; there is nothing here for the ballad-makers, which is the point.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism: FAITH → FAITH
text: {temple}'s take is up and its congregation is down, and {settlement}'s roster carries a second congregation the ledger noticed a good while before the pulpit did.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism: FAITH → FAITH
text: The old rite keeps the nave and the newer keeps the crypt; both halves claim {creed}, both send to the same chapter house, and neither will call itself the new thing.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism: FAITH → FAITH
text: You will be asked which observance you want before you are told where to find it.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism: FAITH → FAITH
text: The parish here remembers a render forgiven once, in a worse year than this, and has never let it go, which is why the argument went to the altar instead of to the steward, and why arithmetic could not settle it.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism: FAITH → FAITH
text: {timeband_since}, the register carries two entries under one name, under a clerk's note nobody has ever settled and nobody is in a hurry to.

kind: JF-F-tithe_to_schism: FAITH → FAITH
text: {settlement} keeps one rite and did not choose to: there was no room here for a second, the weaker congregation was gone before the next observance, {temple} absorbed what was left, and nobody here calls that a reconciliation.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground: FAITH → FAITH
text: The roster at {settlement} restores {creed} to standing directly beneath the entry calling it extinguished; the earlier entry is uncorrected, and nobody has proposed correcting it.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground: FAITH → FAITH
text: Nobody in this parish is a stranger to the ministers who came forward when the suppression lifted.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground: FAITH → FAITH
text: {settlement} will tell you it put {creed} down; the pews have been telling you otherwise since the doors opened again.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground: FAITH → FAITH
text: The elders here call the purge the mistake and say it twice over, for being thorough and for being public: the watching crowd went home knowing more of {creed} than it had come with.

kind: JF-F-suppression_to_underground: FAITH → FAITH
text: {creed}'s share here has risen since the making of the example, and {timeband_since} the seat has made no further examples of anything.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy: FAITH → FAITH
text: {temple}'s standing at {settlement} sits below where it stood before the {calamity}, and the ledger closes the reading failed. The entry is against the namer, not against the season.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy: FAITH → FAITH
text: The parish here remembers being told which season it would lift, and paid the penance for the telling. The season came, and went, and the pulpit has stopped mentioning it.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy: FAITH → FAITH
text: Nobody in {settlement} will read you an omen without being asked twice.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy: FAITH → FAITH
text: The older parishioners point out that nobody here asked whether the harvest failed for weather; they asked whose fault it was, and were answered.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy: FAITH → FAITH
text: The next reading out of that pulpit is weighed against this one before it is finished, and {rival_creed}'s ministers preach against a promise they never had to make.

kind: JF-F-omen_to_failed_prophecy: FAITH → FAITH
text: {temple}'s standing at {settlement} sits where it stood or better, and the same {calamity} crossed this parish and the next on one wind; here it was called patience, the ledger closed the reading fulfilled, and {timeband_since} the sceptics have had nothing cheap to say.

kind: JF-P-boom_to_bust: POP → POP
text: The roll at {settlement} stands near where it stood before the road filled: the town sent {band} down the {route} at the sowing and has most of them back.

kind: JF-P-boom_to_bust: POP → POP
text: {settlement} is short of its young and getting them back by the road: they went out on a report of work and {good}, and the letters came home before the people did and did not speak of {good} at all.

kind: JF-P-boom_to_bust: POP → POP
text: The {route} out of {settlement} runs quiet where it used to run full.

kind: JF-P-boom_to_bust: POP → POP
text: The elders at {settlement} can still point to where the voice stood that emptied the road: it named {counterpart} once, nobody here had seen that town's {good}, and nobody doubted it either.

kind: JF-P-boom_to_bust: POP → POP
text: {timeband_since}, {settlement} still hears the name {counterpart} as a warning rather than as a place.

kind: JF-P-boom_to_bust: POP → POP
text: The stores at {settlement} are counted at the gate and the count refused the column that came for them; the gate was held by men who had to look at them while they held it, and {band} were back on the {route} before the market day came round.

kind: JF-P-petition_to_riot: POP → POP
text: {settlement} is still counting what that night cost and the paper that asked first cost nothing at all; the petition over {reason} sits in the book directly above the refusal.

kind: JF-P-petition_to_riot: POP → POP
text: The square is a market again, and was not, in the season the seat's answer failed to come.

kind: JF-P-petition_to_riot: POP → POP
text: The granary gates at {settlement} are new and the granary is not.

kind: JF-P-petition_to_riot: POP → POP
text: The elders here can name the rungs in order: it was a ladder and every one of them was climbed, and they will point out how little was actually carried away.

kind: JF-P-petition_to_riot: POP → POP
text: Nothing was settled and the streets are quiet; the memory does the work the crowd did, and {timeband_since} the seat still weighs a call twice before it makes one.

kind: JF-P-petition_to_riot: POP → POP
text: {settlement} carries a grievance that closed in the hall where it opened: the seat answered at the first rung, the ledger shows what the answering drained, and it is cheaper by every reckoning than the granary gate.

kind: JF-P-exodus_to_refounding: POP → POP
text: {settlement}'s roll carries {band} of arrivals out of {counterpart} and no clerk here had to ask where from: the tie the departure wrote is the same one the road runs back along.

kind: JF-P-exodus_to_refounding: POP → POP
text: The street version at {settlement} is that the people were sent and not lost, and that {counterpart} owes for the sending; nobody here has decided when to present the bill.

kind: JF-P-exodus_to_refounding: POP → POP
text: New work sits on old foundations here, because the old ones were the shape somebody still had.

kind: JF-P-exodus_to_refounding: POP → POP
text: The {temple} at {settlement} still reads the roll of the ones who took the {route} at the turning of the season, and a house that lost its people to {counterpart} will not lend to {counterpart}.

kind: JF-P-exodus_to_refounding: POP → POP
text: The road fills along an entry rather than along a wage, which is why the clerks never have to ask where from, and {timeband_since} the band between the two towns has not thinned.

kind: JF-P-exodus_to_refounding: POP → POP
text: The rows for {counterpart} are all still in {settlement}'s book and nothing reads them: the names stopped being said at the turning of the season, the band crossed to none, and nothing will read them again.

kind: JF-I-lure_to_war: INFO → INFO
text: {counterpart}'s clerks hold the telling and the forger's price in one file with the buyer's name written underneath, and {timeband_since} {settlement} is still answering for it in {counterpart}'s courts.

kind: JF-I-lure_to_war: INFO → INFO
text: The muster at {settlement} is stood down and the town has not decided yet whether that is a relief or a humiliation; the story it was raised on broke first.

kind: JF-I-lure_to_war: INFO → INFO
text: {settlement} keeps a heavy watch on the {route} road against a muster that has already stood down: the count that raised it was sold to {faction}, and it has been contradicted since.

kind: JF-I-lure_to_war: INFO → INFO
text: Nobody in the council can say even now who brought the count in. The older hands hold that this was the tell, and hold it only in hindsight.

kind: JF-I-lure_to_war: INFO → INFO
text: The tale is still in circulation at {settlement} and still unused: the captains had it and had better word off two roads besides, the live muster showed an equal host, the march was refused on the count, and the coin that paid for the telling is not coming back.

kind: JF-I-plant_to_backfire: INFO → INFO
text: {house}'s stamp out of {settlement} is worth {band} less with {reason} written beside it in every counting-house that keeps one; two tellings out of it could not both be true, and both were on paper.

kind: JF-I-plant_to_backfire: INFO → INFO
text: The market that sold the story is wearing it: {settlement} kept the coin and lost the custom, and can tell you to the quay which custom.

kind: JF-I-plant_to_backfire: INFO → INFO
text: Word out of {settlement} arrives later than it used to, and nothing out of it arrives alone.

kind: JF-I-plant_to_backfire: INFO → INFO
text: The bill is not paid at once and never stops being paid; the older factors take {house}'s word in writing where they once took it across a table.

kind: JF-I-plant_to_backfire: INFO → INFO
text: {timeband_since}, the thing travels on its own, and the note recording who made it travels in the same packet, so every fresh use of it is a fresh airing of {house}'s name.

kind: JF-I-plant_to_backfire: INFO → INFO
text: Nothing in {settlement}'s books carries a mark from the bought story: it arrived at a court already better served off two roads, agreed with neither, and thinned and stopped. {house} was paid all the same, because the coin bought a telling and could not buy a believing.

kind: JF-I-courier_to_treason: INFO → INFO
text: Both tellings are filed together at {settlement}, the false one first and the true one beneath it, and the gap between the ruling and the clearing word is in the record and has been left there.

kind: JF-I-courier_to_treason: INFO → INFO
text: The seat is asking which road it paid for: two accounts of one parlay came in by two roads and did not agree, and that is the whole of what anybody here can say.

kind: JF-I-courier_to_treason: INFO → INFO
text: {settlement} sends two now, and reads them together, and pays for both.

kind: JF-I-courier_to_treason: INFO → INFO
text: The town goes on living beside both families: the sweep caught what sweeps catch (some of it the channel, some of it a neighbour with a grudge and a name to offer), and the false accusation stands as reputation and as nothing more.

kind: JF-I-courier_to_treason: INFO → INFO
text: The seat acted on {reason} and learned better, and the acting cannot be taken back. No one lied here; the road was simply faster with one telling than with the other.

kind: JF-G-signed_to_lapse: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: Nothing written stands between {settlement} and {counterpart}: the {term} reached its date and the clerks struck it, and the book is the only place it was mourned.

kind: JF-G-signed_to_lapse: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: Nobody at {settlement} calls it a breach and nobody ever had to: the wagons came a little short and then a little shorter, through {timeband_span}, and the clerks weighed what arrived against what was promised until the ledger would not close.

kind: JF-G-signed_to_lapse: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: The {route} is open again, to anything at all; where a treaty stood there is distance and custom now, and custom binds nobody.

kind: JF-G-signed_to_lapse: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: The {term} is {timeband_age} and no hand that signed it still holds a seat; the market cannot name one of them.

kind: JF-G-signed_to_lapse: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: There is nothing left to renew and nobody moving to renew it: the window opened, the chancery let the season pass, and the clerks entered that as a decision because there was nothing else to enter it as.

kind: JF-G-signed_to_lapse: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: The {term} between {settlement} and {counterpart} still stands, re-cut rather than let go: a mediator sat the two courts down over a pact neither had broken, and the terms {settlement} argued itself hoarse over are the ones it keeps.

kind: JF-G-succession_to_repudiation: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: Every term under the treaty with {counterpart} is defaulted from the week {npc} said so, and the parchment is kept at {settlement} only as evidence.

kind: JF-G-succession_to_repudiation: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: The town remarks that nothing was seized and nothing was burned: the renunciation was read out in the square, and the clerks defaulted the {term} before the square had emptied.

kind: JF-G-succession_to_repudiation: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: Courts have begun pricing what a promise out of {settlement} is worth, and they are pricing it low.

kind: JF-G-succession_to_repudiation: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: This house has disavowed {band} times before, and the entry has sat {timeband_since} in every chancery that keeps such entries.

kind: JF-G-succession_to_repudiation: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: The next proposal out of {settlement} will be refused on the credibility rather than on the terms, and there will be no arguing it, because there are no terms to argue.

kind: JF-G-succession_to_repudiation: GRAMMAR → GRAMMAR
text: The treaty with {counterpart} stands, and stands because nobody spoke: no word came from the new seat there and the date passed, which is what the law reads silence as, and {settlement}'s captains declined to believe it for as long as they were able.

kind: JF-N-strain_to_coup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: {settlement}'s book carries two columns and joins neither: the instalments to {counterpart} left on time, every time, and the standing of the seat that sent them fell over the very same seasons.

kind: JF-N-strain_to_coup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: {burden} stands on {settlement} and the standing of the seat that pays has fallen over the same seasons, and it is the hall that has joined the two: the book carries the columns and no line between them, and the book is what was read out at the verdict.

kind: JF-N-strain_to_coup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: A stranger at {settlement} will hear several accounts of what the town pays {counterpart} and no two alike; the terms are sealed, and the town has filled the gap with its own arithmetic.

kind: JF-N-strain_to_coup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: The older hands hold that the bill was another court's and say so without expecting to be believed: {npc} paid what a treaty required {settlement} to pay, and it cost {npc} the seat.

kind: JF-N-strain_to_coup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: The hall at {settlement} has been quiet for as long as the muster has been full, and the quiet is not agreement; the men who would have carried a motion against the seat are carrying spears, and nobody has had to find out yet what they would have said.

kind: JF-N-strain_to_coup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: Here the fall has a named cause and the clerks can point to the week: the seat lost standing for {reason}, exposed and entered, and the tribute and the war stood exactly where they had stood.

kind: JF-N-burial_to_digup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: The rows against {counterpart} are in {settlement}'s book and are not counted when the hall counts {counterpart}: the war party can read them and cannot cite them, and the standing grievance reads {band} lighter for it.

kind: JF-N-burial_to_digup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: The town has never stopped arguing about which cost more, the grain or the pride: the price was read out in the square before witnesses who will outlive the seat that swore it.

kind: JF-N-burial_to_digup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: {settlement} will tell you the quarrel is buried. {counterpart} has buried nothing, and a decree binds only the hall that made it.

kind: JF-N-burial_to_digup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: {faction} has waited in the open since the decree was read, and the elders here know the difference between a grudge that is closed and one that is merely uncited.

kind: JF-N-burial_to_digup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: A later hall at {counterpart} cited the rows anyway, word for word, and {timeband_since} the old {wound} is back in {settlement}'s book with a new one on top of it for the revoking.

kind: JF-N-burial_to_digup: INTERIOR → INTERIOR
text: {counterpart} keeps its quarrel and {settlement} keeps the receipt: the price was paid in full against the wrong account (the carts went and were taken and thanked for), and the {temple} that witnessed the swearing has been asked about it twice since.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: Piety at {settlement} falls to {band}: no crisis, no scandal, only a long good season.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {temple} counts fewer at the rail each quarter, and the crossing is entered.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: A burned church holds its flock for years. {settlement}'s has finally let go.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {temple}'s candles last longer at {settlement} than they used to.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The offerings at {settlement} are thin, and were thin last quarter.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The holy days at {settlement} are kept by the shops for the morning and by the rest not at all.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {temple} has stopped ringing the lesser hours; nobody was coming to them.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: Observance at {settlement} is {band}, and the ministers have made their peace with it.

kind: faith.piety.crossing_down (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: Nothing happened at {settlement}. That is what a long good season does to a parish.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {creed} and {rival_creed} contested the lesser niche at {settlement}; {creed} keeps it, and the seat is untouched.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The quarrel at {settlement} was over a niche, not the altar (which did not make it quieter).

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {temple} lost the funerary rite at {settlement} to {rival_creed} and kept everything else.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: Neither creed came near the patron seat at {settlement}, and both spent a season trying.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The dispute at {settlement} was over who blesses the boats, and it went to the seat to settle.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {rival_creed} undercut {temple} on burial fees at {settlement}, which decided more than the preaching did.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The roster at {settlement} records the niche changing hands and records no cause.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {creed} keeps the lesser rite at {settlement} for now, and both houses expect to have this out again.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: It was not about the altar. It was never going to be about the altar.

kind: faith.niche.contest (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: Guild men at {settlement} were asked which house they preferred, and answered by custom rather than conviction.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {settlement} has widened its tolerance; the foreign rites may keep their feasts within the walls.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The ledger at {settlement} opens a slot: {faction} judged the quarrel more expensive than the creed.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {npc} argued for the strangers' rite at {settlement}, and was heard.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The doors at {settlement} are open a little wider this year, and nobody has said why.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: Foreign carriers at {settlement} have been given leave to hire a room and use it.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The gate men at {settlement} have new instructions about strangers with vessels.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: {faction} counted what the closed door was costing in trade, and opened it.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: There will be rites kept in {settlement} within the decade that nobody there can name today.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: The old families at {settlement} are not pleased, and are not being consulted.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_open (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: routine
text: Travellers say {settlement} is an easier town to keep a rite in than it was.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_close (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: {settlement} has narrowed its tolerance; the foreign rites keep their feasts outside the walls or not at all.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_close (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: The ledger at {settlement} closes a slot ({reason}), and {creed}'s carriers are turning back at the gate.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_close (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: {faction} has decided {settlement} keeps too many calendars.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_close (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: Nothing is forbidden at {settlement}. It is only made difficult.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_close (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: The rooms the foreign rites hired at {settlement} have been let to other trades.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_close (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: {settlement}'s ledger closes the slot and names {reason}; the clerk wrote it without comment.

kind: faith.tolerance.shift_close (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: Carriers of {creed} go round {settlement} now rather than through it.

kind: faith.mandate.band_move (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: The seat at {settlement} holds its mandate {band}; {temple}'s blessing is doing the work the treasury cannot.

kind: faith.mandate.band_move (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: {temple} has withdrawn its countenance from {settlement}'s seat, and {creed}'s mandate has moved with it.

kind: faith.mandate.band_move (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: The divine mandate at {settlement} stands {band}. The crossing is entered, and the court has felt it.

kind: faith.mandate.band_move (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: {npc} did not attend the seat's investiture at {settlement}, and everyone counted the empty chair.

kind: faith.mandate.band_move (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: The seat's proclamations at {settlement} are read from the temple steps again, which they were not last year.

kind: faith.mandate.band_move (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: {temple}'s blessing is entered on the seat's roll at {band}, and the court reads the roll.

kind: faith.mandate.band_move (WF-8) — Herald `faith` — significance: notable
text: What the seat at {settlement} may ask of the parish has moved with the mandate, and both sides have felt it.

kind: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm is split over {creed}: {settlement} keeps a seat and {counterpart} keeps another, and both send letters.

kind: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: A schism runs the length of the realm; every court has been asked to choose, and most have.

kind: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed}'s houses no longer recognise one another's ministers, and the roads carry rival legates.

kind: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.schism (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm keeps a single faith, and keeps it twice.

kind: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm is on the road: every shrine of {creed} is drawing many hundreds, and the inns cannot hold them.

kind: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: A great pilgrimage season: {route} and every road like it carries the faithful, and the tolls have never been better.

kind: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {temple} has opened its granaries to travellers, and so has every house of {creed} between {settlement} and {counterpart}.

kind: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.great_pilgrimage (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm's roads have not been this busy since the last war, and this time nobody is armed.

kind: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: A coordinated proscription across the realm: {creed}'s houses are closed from {settlement} to {counterpart}.

kind: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The seats have agreed among themselves about {creed}, and the agreement is being enforced street by street.

kind: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed}'s ministers are on the roads, and the roads are watched.

kind: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.persecution (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm has decided {creed} is a danger. The realm has decided this before.

kind: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm's naves are filling. The unaffiliated are coming back, and nobody arranged it.

kind: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: An awakening across the realm: {creed} and {rival_creed} both report crowds, which is how everyone knows it is not a schism.

kind: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: Crisis calls the faithful home, and the {calamity} has called many hundreds.

kind: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.awakening (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The registers are running out of room for names, and the ministers are frankly baffled.

kind: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: A reformation in the realm: patrons have fallen {reason} at {settlement}, at {counterpart}, and beyond, all inside a handful of years.

kind: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm has unseated its patrons by the same argument in parish after parish.

kind: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: A single cause, many falls. The chroniclers will give this a name, and the parishes will give it another.

kind: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.reformation (WF-8, new arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed} is not the only patron to fall {reason} this decade, and the realm is beginning to notice the pattern.

kind: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed} is ascendant across the realm, and the faithful walk the roads in numbers.

kind: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed} is ascendant across the realm; its calendar is kept from {settlement} to {counterpart}.

kind: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The realm's seats keep {creed}'s feasts, and the seats that do not are noticed.

kind: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed} holds its tier by the plain arithmetic of seats, and holds it comfortably.

kind: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.ascendancy (WF-8, existing arc — carries the honesty fork) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: There is no court in the realm where {creed}'s minister waits long for an audience.

kind: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The twilight of {creed}: the seats have fallen away one after another, and the pantheon keeps a title with nothing under it.

kind: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed} has slipped a tier; the realm register records the fall, and the parishes record nothing at all.

kind: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: The great feasts of {creed} are kept in fewer places each year, and kept smaller where they are kept.

kind: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_FAITH.md :: faith.realm.twilight (WF-8, existing arc) — Chronicle (realm register) — significance: major
text: {creed}'s house at {settlement} was the last that mattered, and it does not matter now.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.faith_converted (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {settlement} keeps {rival_creed} now, and keeps it as though it always had.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.faith_converted (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The conversion is complete at {settlement}: the seat, the calendar, and the burying ground.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.faith_converted (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {creed} has no share worth the name at {settlement}; the chronicle closes the entry converted.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.faith_converted (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: A generation ago {settlement} would have been scandalised. A generation is all it took.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.hollowed (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {creed} keeps the seat at {settlement} and almost nothing else; the rite is law and habit and not much more.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.hollowed (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The pews at {settlement} are thin and the roster is unchanged. Hollowed, the chronicle calls it.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.hollowed (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {temple} still rings the hour at {settlement}, and fewer set their day by it each year.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.hollowed (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: Nobody left {creed} at {settlement}. They simply stopped arriving.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.gone_underground (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {creed} is finished at {settlement}, publicly; the chronicle closes it gone to the cellars.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.gone_underground (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The proscription held at {settlement} and the faith did not end. It moved.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.gone_underground (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {settlement}'s register carries {creed} extinguished, and the register is wrong.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.gone_underground (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: They took the building, the vessels, and the calendar, and did not get the congregation.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.resurgent (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {creed} holds {settlement} again, after the suppression and the cellar years; the chronicle closes it resurgent.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.resurgent (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: What was proscribed at {settlement} is established at {settlement}: the same rite, the same families, a new roof.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.resurgent (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {temple} has been reconsecrated at {settlement}, and the crowd knew the responses without prompting.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.resurgent (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: It took a decade and a change of seat. It did not take a miracle, and nobody has claimed one.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.extinct (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {creed} is gone from {settlement} entirely: no seat, no cellar, no memory in the roster.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.extinct (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The chronicle closes {creed} at {settlement}: extinct, and the last to keep it is not named.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.extinct (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The undercroft at {temple} holds grain now, and the plate is said to have gone to the mint.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.extinct (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: There is nobody at {settlement} to be the last of them, which is what extinct means.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.split (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {settlement} ends the age with both congregations standing: the nave and the crypt, and neither yielding.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.split (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The split at {settlement} held; the chronicle closes it split, which is the rarest of the endings and the least tidy.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.split (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {temple}'s roster carries {creed} and {rival_creed} both at {settlement}, impaired and tolerated, into the next generation.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.split (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: They never reconciled at {settlement}. They merely grew accustomed.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.communion (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {creed} and {rival_creed} end in communion. The compact at {settlement} outlasted the quarrel that made it necessary.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.communion (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The shared rite at {settlement} is older than anyone who remembers the war; the chronicle closes it communion.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.communion (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: Both houses keep the feast at {settlement}, and neither can now say which of them started it.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.communion (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The instrument has not been read aloud in years. Nobody has needed to.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.imposed_held (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {rival_creed} came to {settlement} with {faction}'s garrison and is still there after the garrison left.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.imposed_held (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: The imposed rite held at {settlement}. The chronicle closes it imposed and kept, which is not the same as chosen.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.imposed_held (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: {settlement}'s children keep {rival_creed} and do not remember it arriving.

section: §M WF-9 — THE ENDINGS MIX (the closed eight)
kind: faith.ending.imposed_held (WF-9) — Chronicle — significance: major
text: They knelt because they were told to. Their grandchildren kneel because it is what one does.

kind: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_GRAMMAR.md :: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
text: The peace of {settlement} and {counterpart} has run its course: {band} years, and no hand that signed it still holds a seat.

kind: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_GRAMMAR.md :: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
text: The {term} {settlement} and {counterpart} kept between them came to its last day and was filed as closed; neither court sent word, and the clerks who closed it were the only ones who marked it.

kind: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_GRAMMAR.md :: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
text: In {settlement} the market kept its hours as always; the pact with {counterpart} ended that week, and the carters heard of it after the clerks.

kind: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_GRAMMAR.md :: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
text: {settlement} and {counterpart} are bound by nothing now. The {term} ran out, and neither court asked for another.

kind: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
pool: RECEIPT_POOLS_GRAMMAR.md :: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
text: It was written for {band} years and it kept every one of them; both courts let it go without a word.

kind: treaty_lapsed (GR-0) — Herald / chronicle (the eulogy) — significance: notable
